subject: Performance playbook for close ramp — concurrency & model selection
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@integracare.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance playbook & test plan for Integracare MAP (initial)

Claire — thanks for taking time on the call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is the draft Mutual Action Plan and the performance playbook we'll run during the close ramp. High-level ask: confirm acceptance criteria for latency and throughput so we can pick the model variant and sizing that hits your product SLAs.

Key target metrics (please confirm):
- Primary SLO: TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 120ms p50 for 1k concurrent chat sessions
- Tail latency: p99 <= 800ms under steady-state traffic
- Throughput: sustain 18k tokens/sec at peak (all pods combined)
- Concurrency targets to test: 64, 256, 512 concurrent sessions per region
- Quality: automated QA pass rate >= 92% on your triage prompts (we'll run your 250 prompt set)

Planned test matrix (short):
- Variants: rwd-6b-int8 (cost-optimized), rwd-13b-q4_1 (balanced), rwd-30b-ffn-run (quality-first)
- Quantization: int8 vs q4_1 profiles
- Config knobs: batching window (5-20ms), KV cache warmup, dynamic batching thresholds

Schedule (proposed):
1) 2026-11-02: run baseline throughput and TTFT at concurrency 64
2) 2026-11-03: stress runs at 256 and 512, measure p50/p95/p99 and token/sec
3) 2026-11-04: quality evaluation on your 250 prompt set (automated + 20 human checks)
4) 2026-11-05: internal recommendation + MAP update; vendor PO target 2026-11-12

Deliverables: test results CSV, variant recommendation doc, updated MAP with rollout plan and fallbacks.

If that looks right, please reply with any changes. If you want lower TTFT priority (favoring throughput/cost), say so and we'll adapt the matrix.

Thanks — Jonas

jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

Subject: Re: Performance playbook & test plan for Integracare MAP (initial)

Thanks Jonas — this looks thorough and aligns with our objectives. A couple notes from the product team:
- TTFT is priority over sustained throughput for the triage flow — patient wait experience matters more than long-form throughput.
- We want p95 <= 450ms if possible; p99 relaxable to 900ms only during peak bursts.
- For quality, the 250 prompt set is fine; we'll add 30 high-risk prompts (sensitive phrasing) by tomorrow EOD.

We're available for testing on Nov 2–4 as you proposed. Procurement is aiming to finalize PO the week of Nov 8; earlier confirmation from you will help.

Claire

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T18:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Performance playbook & test plan — results (draft)

Quick summary of runs completed today (attached full CSV: stress_results_20261103.csv). Tests ran against Integracare prompt set (250 auto + 30 high-risk). All runs were with a warm KV cache unless noted.

Environment notes:
- Dedicated pool: 6 x A100-equivalent pods (reserved by Ben)
- Batching window used: 10ms (default), also tested 5ms and 20ms
- Traffic pattern: steady-state + 30s spike to repro burst behavior

Key numbers (representative):
Variant: rwd-6b-int8 (cost) — best cost per token
- TTFT p50: 85ms
- p95: 420ms
- p99: 930ms
- Sustained throughput: 22k tokens/sec (6 pods)
- QA pass rate: 88% (failed mostly on nuance prompts)

Variant: rwd-13b-q4_1 (balanced) — recommended default
- TTFT p50: 115ms
- p95: 360ms
- p99: 740ms
- Sustained throughput: 14k tokens/sec (6 pods)
- QA pass rate: 94%

Variant: rwd-30b-ffn-run (quality-first)
- TTFT p50: 190ms
- p95: 600ms
- p99: 1300ms
- Sustained throughput: 7k tokens/sec (6 pods)
- QA pass rate: 97%

Concurrency behavior (selected):
- At 64 concurrent sessions: all variants meet p50/p95 targets; rwd-6b shows highest throughput headroom.
- At 256: rwd-6b-int8 p99 jumps >1.2s for some bursts; rwd-13b-q4_1 still within p99 800ms most of the time.
- At 512: only rwd-6b-int8 with aggressive batching hit throughput target but at the cost of p99 >1.5s; rwd-13b requires +2 pods to maintain p99 <900ms.

Runtime knobs that helped:
- Reducing batching window to 5ms lowered TTFT by ~12ms at a small throughput cost.
- Prefix caching of the common system prompt reduced token generation by ~8% across runs.

Recommendation: rwd-13b-q4_1 as the primary model for Integracare's triage flow; standby fallback rwd-6b-int8 for sustainable cost saving on off-peak hours or for batch offline jobs. If Integracare insists on the tightest TTFT at peak, we can provision +2 pods (cost impact ~+22% monthly).

Next steps: I'll upload the CSV and a short variant_summary PDF to Drive and link into the MAP. Jonas — if this aligns, propose the close timeline and I'll help populate the technical acceptance criteria in the MAP doc.

—Marissa

Short TL;DR from the runs:
- Best balance: rwd-13b-q4_1 meets Integracare quality bar (94% QA) while keeping p99 within the target with the proposed Dedicated pool.
- If TTFT absolute minimum is your priority (p50 <100ms across peaks), we can configure rwd-6b-int8 as a fallback for read-only triage micro-flows or provision +2 pods at steady state.

Proposed MAP/close timeline:
- Nov 5: Redwood finalizes MAP with tech acceptance criteria (Marissa to populate).
- Nov 8: Integracare legal/procurement sign-off window opens.
- Nov 12: Preferred PO date to enable provisioning before Nov 16 pilot.

Please confirm you are comfortable with rwd-13b-q4_1 as the primary variant and whether you'd like the low-latency fallback (rwd-6b-int8) active on a schedule (off-peak) or only as emergency fallback. Once you confirm, procurement and I will finalize contract language and pricing.

Thanks — Jonas
